newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Development wins Taiwan financial centre bid.
newsitem.headline: China Development wins Taiwan financial centre bid.

text.p: A consortium led by Taiwan's China Development Corp won the bidding to build an international financial centre in in central Taipei, city government officials said on Saturday.
"China Development won the bidding of the Taipei International Financial Building with a price of T$20.689 billion," Taipei city government secretary-general Liao Cheng-chin said after the auction.
China Development defeated six other competitors with a bid that was double the base price of T$10.3 billion, officials said.

China Development Corp is a venture capital firm backed by Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party -- one of the world's wealthiest political parties with a total of asset of over T$85 billion (US$3.09 billion) at the end of December 1996.
The consortium it led included China Life Insurance, Cathay Life Insurance, Shin Kong Life Insurance and Cathay Construction, and Walsin Lihwa.
Taipei's municipal government still has the ownership of the land but China Development would be entitled to use the land for 70 years.
"Given the land's future economic potential, we feel the bidding price is fairly reasonable," China Development official Kung Shen-you told reporters.
Analysts said the result indicated a gradual bottoming-out of the property market.

Taiwan's real estate market had been sluggish since it reached a peak in 1989. Recent economic indicators and gradually improving sales had indicated a gradually recovering real estate market, analysts said.
In June, unlisted Nan Shan Life Insurance Co bought a big piece of state land in Taipei's commercial district in an auction with a price of T$2.72 billion, or 40 percent higher than the base price.
The central bank said loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms grew 0.80 percent to T$404.230 billion year on year in May, marking the first rise in two years.
